summary.title: As an employee of a startup, how do you know when to quit?
summary.one_liner: Learn how to tell whether a startup is failing or you are the problem, using a "are you getting more than you give" test, company-level warning signs, personal-fit checks, and a rough expected-value method for deciding when to leave.
keywords: knowing when to leave a job
takeaways: Ask whether you are getting more from the company than it gets from you; when the balance tips, start looking.
Separate objective company signals (missed milestones, hidden metrics, insolvency, unethical conduct) from personal-fit signals (skill gaps, burnout, role mismatch).
Run short experiments such as a 30–90 day plan with measurable objectives and check whether the company responds.
Estimate opportunity cost and expected payoff in rough numbers to judge whether staying is still rational.
Leave immediately for unscrupulous deals, toxic culture, or demands that damage your health; never stay just to protect sunk costs.
summary.summary: This is a Quora thread collecting answers from many startup employees and founders to the question of when to leave a startup and how to tell company problems from a personal lack of grit. Contributors share personal stories, rules of thumb (such as a "gets more vs gives more" test and a 3-month unhappiness rule), and an opportunity-cost calculation. One answer adds a structured checklist covering company signals, personal-fit signals, diagnostic questions, practical 30–90 day tests, and an exit execution list. The answers vary in rigor, so the structured checklist is the most systematic part.
